rubric: One element is clearly read first: the headline is much larger than the body text and nothing else competes with it.
There is exactly one primary call to action; the secondary link is visibly quieter than the button.
The paragraph under the headline has a comfortable line length (about 40 to 75 characters) and secondary text still has strong contrast against its background.
Spacing groups the headline, paragraph and buttons as one unit, with generous whitespace and consistent alignment of edges.
The product visual looks specific to an invoice-reminder tool and supports the message without competing with the headline.

result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): The two heroes share almost the same headline, paragraph and layout, so the decision comes down to the calls to action and the product visual. A has a dark 'Start free' button in the nav that competes with the main free-trial button, and its dashboard (stats row, toast and email overlay) is busier and pulls attention from the headline. B has a single primary button and a calmer invoice list with an email card, but that card awkwardly covers row amounts and due dates. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A has one clear primary CTA. B's dark 'Start free' button in the nav competes with the hero button, and B's busier dashboard, with stats, a toast and a card spilling toward the copy, pulls more attention from the headline. B's visual is richer and more polished, but A's email popover clips the amount and status in one row, which looks a little unfinished. Even so, A follows the hierarchy goals more closely.
